summary: The candidate-5 runtime controls remain fail-closed: all five artifact schemas are closed at every declared object node; model-response key/type mutations fail; canonical progress bytes, committed-history replay, rollback, artifact hashes, and progress-commit/derived-seal binding passed focused controls. One candidate-5 regression remains in committed evidence: the packet additional-property mutation test was repurposed into a prompt-only preflight test, so a source-packet root-schema loosening mutant now survives all 93 mutation tests even though the current schema itself is still strict.

findings.title: Candidate 5 removes the committed source-packet additional-property mutation kill
findings.claim: scripts/test_correctness_audit_mutations.py::test_packet_semantic_field_rejected_by_schema no longer enters validate() or asserts the source-packet schema diagnostic. It now asserts only that canonical_prompt_bytes rejects the downstream-only key physicalClass, while retaining a schema-specific test name. Consequently, changing source-packet.schema.json root additionalProperties from false to true survives the entire candidate-5 93-test mutation suite. The same mutant was killed by the prior-head version of this test.

evidence.detail: Candidate 5 dumps a packet containing physicalClass and expects canonical_prompt_bytes to raise forbidden identifier key physicalClass; it does not resign the chain, run the public validator, or assert Additional properties are not allowed.
The candidate replaces resign_packet_chain plus assertFails(Additional properties are not allowed) with the prompt-preflight assertion.

Temporary candidate-5 clone with only source-packet root additionalProperties loosened. All 93 mutation tests passed, including the still-named schema test. A neutral unexpectedPacketField then passed the full no-seal validator with failureCount 0, confirming the mutant weakens the strict packet contract rather than being equivalent.

The equivalent prior-head mutant made the prior test exit 1 because the expected Additional properties are not allowed failure disappeared; the remaining prompt-token failure did not satisfy that assertion.

findings.impact: The current candidate schema still has additionalProperties false and independently rejects extra packet fields, so this is a committed regression-control defect rather than a presently exploitable schema acceptance. Future or accidental root-schema loosening is no longer killed by the advertised 93-test mutation suite, and candidate-4 strict-schema evidence is carried forward without acknowledging that its packet-schema guard was replaced.
findings.minimalFix: Keep the new physicalClass prompt-preflight test, rename it for that purpose, and add a separate public-validator test using a neutral unknown packet key such as unexpectedPacketField. Re-sign the chain and require the Additional properties are not allowed schema failure. Add a root additionalProperties mutant control so the mutation suite proves it kills the loosening.

A valid baseline -> direct artifact seal -> progress transition history passed. A canonical semantic no-op with reordered top-level bytes failed as noncanonical. Existing one-step, timestamp, count, unchanged-row, and merge controls remained green in the 93-test suite.
A forced post-write validation failure emitted transition rolled back and restored progress.json byte-for-byte.

The updater writes in place and restores bytes on ordinary validation exceptions; crash, power-loss, or partial-filesystem-write atomicity remains unproved and was already documented before candidate 5.
